description:
FILED s399 (Opus 5) while doing the ASK-1 internals registration
(fable-answers-s396.md §4): found by the per-row read the registration bar
demands, on op/const-optree.t.  Occurs as 4 FAILING ROWS in that file, so it is
not a pure filler -- and it is what keeps op/const-optree.t UNEXPLAINED (see
docs/not-supported.md §Readouts of perl's own internals ->
"Constant-folding / inlinability").

PCL compiles `my sub NAME {...}` as a PACKAGE sub.  Two lexical subs of the
same name in DIFFERENT scopes therefore clobber each other, and every `\&NAME`
resolves to whichever was defined LAST.  Silent: no warning, no die, a wrong
value.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3 (scratchpad lexsub3.pl):

    use feature 'lexical_subs';
    my $g1 = sub { my sub x () { 8 } \&x };
    my $g2 = sub { my sub x () { 3 } \&x };
    print &{$g1->()}, " ", &{$g2->()};
        perl: 8 3          PCL: 3 3      SILENT WRONG

In ISOLATION (one `my sub x` in the file) PCL is right -- which is why this
never showed up before: it needs two same-named lexical subs, exactly what
t/op/const-optree.t has (`my sub with constant` returns 8, `my sub:method with
constant` returns 3, and all four of the first group's retval rows then read 3).

POPULATION: op/const-optree.t rows "retval of my sub with constant",
"... with constant and return", "... with optimised statement and constant",
"... with optimised statement, constant and return" (4 rows).  op/lexsub.t
(156 rows) is the FEATURE's own file and does not even transpile today -- it
dies in Pl/Parser.pm "Negative repeat count does nothing" (#314 singles list),
so size the two together: this task is the SCOPING half, op/lexsub.t's single
is the PARSE half.

FIX SHAPE (not designed -- measure first): a `my sub` is a LEXICAL, so the
declaration must produce a per-scope name the way the file-lexical rename
passes already produce one for `my $x` (a scope-unique CL symbol), with
`\&NAME` and a bare `NAME()` call inside the scope resolving to it.  Check
whether the existing lexical-rename machinery (Parser2's _rename_* family)
can own it before adding a second mechanism -- CLAUDE.md #11.  `state sub`
and `our sub` are the siblings; probe all three.

BAR: probe ~10 shapes vs perl (nested scopes, recursion through the lexical
name, a same-named package sub in scope, \&NAME identity across two calls,
redefinition in an inner block); corpus-diff; gate; and because it is a name-
resolution change, the full sweep (the s386/#296 rule: a rename/scoping change
takes the sweep as its gate).  Then re-measure op/const-optree.t and revisit
its registration.


PROBE BATTERY RUN s406 (12 shapes, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL; scratchpad lexsub/p*.pl).
The task asked for ~10 before designing — here they are, with PCL's answer:

  shape                                                   perl        PCL
  1  two anon scopes, `my sub x` each, \&x from both      8 3         3 3     WRONG (#337 core)
  2  pkg sub + `my sub nm` in a block (p2b.pl)            LEX PKG     LEX LEX WRONG (clobber)
  3  nested `my sub f` shadowing an outer one             inner outer inner inner WRONG
  4  recursion through the lexical name (`my sub rec`)    DIES        rrr     PCL is MORE permissive (principle 9) — but op/lexsub.t asserts the die
  5  same with `state sub`                                DIES        rrr     ditto (perl does NOT make it self-visible either, measured)
  6  `our sub o` + main::o()                              OUR OUR     OUR OUR OK
  7  \&f == \&f identity                                  same        diff    DIVERGES — but NOT lexical-sub-specific: a plain package `sub f` diverges identically (project_coderef_identity_blocker), so it is not this task
  8  `my sub h` called twice inside a named sub           H1H2        H1H2    OK
  9  `my sub cap { $x * 2 }` closing over a my var        42          42      OK (captures the CELL, like perl)
 10  `for my $i (1,2) { my sub g { "g$i" } g() }`         g1 g2       TRANSPILE FAILS "Parser2 TODO: lexical 'i' possibly captured by nested sub g"  <-- the #347 family again, in a LOOP body; and even once it compiles, a top-level hoisted CV cannot give perl's fresh-closure-per-iteration
 11  prototype on a lexical sub (`my sub p ($$)`)         1 2         1 2     OK
 12  call BEFORE the declaration (pkg sub in scope)       PKG LEX     LEX LEX WRONG — the rename REGION must start at the declaration, not at the block

SO THE DESIGN, in one line: a per-scope rename whose region runs from the
declaration to the end of the enclosing block and STOPS at a sibling
redeclaration (the #296-B2 rule), rewriting the definition, bare NAME() calls,
&NAME and \&NAME inside it — exactly what the _rename_* family already does for
`my $x`.  Shapes 1/2/3/12 are all that rename.  Shape 10 is a SEPARATE axis
(per-iteration closures) and should be sized on its own, not promised with the
rename.  Shapes 4/5 are principle-9 divergences to register, not to fix.

A side probe found an unrelated silent wrong and filed it: task #361
(`print x(), …` with a sub named `x` reads as the repetition operator).


RULED s407 (fable-answers-s406.md §4.8 ask 4): the SPLIT is confirmed.  Session
F = the rename half only (shapes 1/2/3/12): a per-scope rename whose region runs
from the DECLARATION to the end of the enclosing block and STOPS at a sibling
redeclaration (#296-B2), rewriting the definition, bare NAME() calls, &NAME and
\&NAME — the _rename_* family; the sweep IS the gate.  Shape 10 (fresh closure
per loop iteration) is the SAME residue as #347's registered "will not stay
shared" family: a hoisted named sub cannot be a fresh closure per iteration; the
fix is a promotion-decision change (a per-call cell for the hoisted sub), NOT a
rename — record it on that not-supported.md family, size it separately, do not
promise it with the rename.  Shapes 4/5: register (principle 9).


DONE s408 (Opus 5), commit 7f930fc.  Pl/Parser2::_rename_lexical_subs: each
`my sub` / `state sub` declaration gets a scope-unique name (NAME__lexsub__N)
and the uses its region owns are rewritten.  Region = from the DECLARATION to
the end of the enclosing scope, stopping at a sibling redeclaration (#296-B2).
Nesting needed NO shadow test: a use is claimed by the covering declaration
with the LATEST start, which is by construction the innermost one in scope --
so shapes 1/2/3/12 and the sibling-redecl rule all fall out of one comparison.
Runs in parse() ahead of every name-keyed pass.

WHAT THE DESIGN MISSED, and a probe caught: a rename that rewrites only the
TOKEN STREAM is incomplete.  Interpolated CODE ("@{[ f() ]}", heredocs,
patterns) is compiled from the STRING TEXT, so the embedded call still named
the package sub -- which after the rename does not exist: "the function
main::pl-f is undefined", a crash the pass itself introduced.  Fixed via
Pl::InterpScan (standing rule S8) for the spans + the SAME use-classifier,
applied by parsing each span as Perl; wired through the existing
_fix_interp_token so heredoc bodies and patterns come free.

PROBES: 41 shapes vs perl 5.40.3, 38 identical.  The 3 divergences are all
REGISTERED in docs/not-supported.md (new section "A lexical sub (my sub NAME)
reached from a place that is not the token stream"):
  * a STRING eval cannot see a lexical sub (loud; before the rename it worked
    only because every lexical sub WAS a package sub -- the same accident as
    this bug).  Lifting it = a sub-capture alist on the eval request, sized
    with #364, NOT scheduled.
  * a body call to its own name is accepted where perl DIES (principle 9).
  * shape 10 (fresh closure per loop iteration) -> recorded on the #347
    "will not stay shared" family, as ruled.

MEASURED: gate 147/5359 with only the 13 pclxs xs rows failing, and per-file
IDENTICAL to a HEAD worktree (the written-down 5355 was stale: the xs files
abort at different points as pclxs is worked on).  corpus-diff 3 of 111 differ
(eval.t, sort.t, sub.t), every hunk a name substitution, silent drops 12
unchanged; emission-ab lib 20/20 SAME; FULL SWEEP GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed,
TOTAL 18517 = baseline, drops 12 = census, and the three changed files are
row-for-row at baseline.  Guard Pl/t/lexical-sub-01.t (18 oracle rows, 52 s).

NOT renamed, deliberately: `our sub` (that IS a package sub, probed OK) and a
blockless `my sub b;` predeclaration (it defines nothing; the corpus has it
only inside eval strings, perl-tests/sub.t 427/436).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `my sub NAME` is compiled as a PACKAGE sub -- two same-named lexical subs in different scopes clobber each other (\&x resolves to the last one)
